---
title: "Architecture"
---

Saving `post.qmd` updates the browser in a few milliseconds: no reload, no lost
scroll, no cold start. That is possible because of one decision, drawn in
@fig-architecture: **all of the intelligence lives in the Rust core behind a stable
websocket protocol, and the browser preview is a thin client.**

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-architecture
%%| fig-cap: "Thin clients talk to the server over a websocket; all rendering lives in the Rust core."
flowchart LR
  BR["Browser preview<br/>(vanilla JS)"]
  subgraph Server["qmd-fast server"]
    direction TB
    WS["Websocket<br/>+ file watcher"]
    subgraph Core["qmd-fast-core"]
      direction TB
      P["Parser<br/>comrak + sourcepos"] --> M["Block model<br/>+ diff"] --> R["Render<br/>html / deck / book"]
    end
    K["Warm Jupyter kernel"]
  end
  F[(".qmd files")]
  BR <-->|JSON protocol| WS
  WS --> P
  R -->|changed blocks| WS
  F -.->|watch| WS
  M -->|code cells| K --> M
```

| Component | Crate / path | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Core | `crates/core` | Parsing (comrak + sourcepos), the block model, HTML rendering |
| Server | `crates/server` | Websocket dev server, file watcher, Jupyter kernel pool |
| Web client | `web-client/` | Browser preview client (vanilla JS) |

The protocol is open, so an embedded editor client is a new thin client, not a rewrite:
the in-repo VS Code companion (covered in [extending qmd-fast](extending.qmd)) is exactly
that.

## How a save flows

Change `tau` from 10 to 12 in `post.qmd` and save. That edit flows through the
pipeline as @fig-save-flow shows, and crucially, only the **changed** blocks reach
the preview: the heading and the paragraph stay put, and only the plot the cell
redraws crosses the wire.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-save-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Only the changed blocks are pushed to the preview."
flowchart LR
  save["Save .qmd"] --> watch["File watcher"]
  watch --> parse["Re-parse + block model"]
  parse --> diff["Diff by block id"]
  diff --> ws["Websocket:<br/>changed blocks only"]
  ws --> dom["Preview updates<br/>in place"]
```

The same save as an interaction over time, module by module, is @fig-save-seq:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-save-seq
%%| fig-cap: "A save, module by module: only changed blocks (and re-run cells) cross the wire."
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant FS as .qmd file
  participant SV as serve.rs (watcher)
  participant RN as render/ (core)
  participant EX as exec + kernel
  participant DF as diff.rs
  participant CL as client.js
  FS->>SV: changed (notify)
  SV->>RN: re-render (debounced)
  RN->>EX: run first changed cell + downstream
  EX-->>RN: output blocks
  RN-->>SV: new block list
  SV->>DF: new blocks vs live blocks
  DF-->>SV: BlockOps (changed only)
  SV->>CL: ws update / insert / remove
  CL->>CL: swap blocks in place (scroll + live state kept)
```

The two crates split cleanly: **`qmd-fast-core` does all the thinking and touches
no network** (it parses, models, and renders), while **`qmd-fast-server` is the
long-running process** (CLI, websocket, file watcher, kernel pool). The browser
client is a thin layer that mounts blocks and applies the ops the server sends.

## The codebase map

The dependency shape first, who leans on whom (@fig-modules). The server
orchestrates and owns the runtime; the core does all the rendering and never
touches the network; the browser client only mounts blocks and applies ops.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-modules
%%| fig-cap: "Module dependencies across the three layers (an arrow means 'uses / calls')."
flowchart TB
  subgraph client["web-client/ · browser (vanilla JS)"]
    CL["client.js<br/>mount · apply ops · click-to-source"]
  end

  subgraph server["crates/server · qmd-fast (binary)"]
    direction TB
    MAIN["main.rs · CLI"]
    SRV["serve.rs<br/>single doc"]
    SITE["serve_site.rs<br/>site / book"]
    EX["exec.rs · executor"]
    KR["kernel.rs<br/>warm ZMQ kernel"]
    MAIN --> SRV
    MAIN --> SITE
    SRV --> EX
    SITE --> EX
    EX --> KR
  end

  subgraph core["crates/core · qmd-fast-core (library)"]
    direction TB
    RN["render/<br/>parse → block model → HTML"]
    DF["diff.rs"]
    SM["site/<br/>multi-page projects"]
    INC["includes.rs"]
    FM["frontmatter.rs"]
    CI["cite.rs"]
    MA["math.rs"]
    HL["highlight.rs"]
    RN --> INC
    RN --> FM
    RN --> CI
    RN --> MA
    RN --> HL
    SM --> RN
  end

  CL <-->|ws JSON| SRV
  CL <-->|ws JSON| SITE
  SRV --> RN
  SRV --> DF
  SITE --> SM
  SITE --> DF
  EX -->|output blocks| DF
```

The data those modules pass around is small (@fig-data-model): a `RenderedDoc` is
a list of `Block`s, an executable block carries a `Cell`, and `diff.rs` turns two
block lists into a stream of `BlockOp`s.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-data-model
%%| fig-cap: "The core data model (key fields shown): what flows from the parser to the client."
classDiagram
  class RenderedDoc {
    Option~String~ title
    DocFormat format
    bool toc
    Vec~Warning~ warnings
    Vec~Block~ blocks
  }
  class Block {
    String id
    String sourcepos
    Option~String~ source_file
    String html
    Option~Cell~ cell
  }
  class Cell {
    String lang
    String code
    bool echo
    bool include
  }
  class BlockOp {
    <<enumeration>>
    Update
    Insert
    Remove
    SetMeta
  }
  class Warning {
    String message
    Option~String~ file
    Option~u32~ line
  }
  RenderedDoc "1" *-- "many" Block : blocks
  RenderedDoc "1" o-- "many" Warning : warnings
  Block "1" o-- "0..1" Cell : cell
  Block ..> BlockOp : diff emits
```

With the shape in mind, here is the file-by-file detail, one table per layer.

`crates/core/src`, the library (`qmd-fast-core`):

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `render/mod.rs` | The render pipeline (`render_internal`). The coordinator. |
| `render/model.rs` | The block-model data types (`Cell`, `Block`, `RenderedDoc`, `DocFormat`). |
| `render/page.rs` | Full HTML-page assembly: the `PAGE_TEMPLATE` shell, site-chrome wiring, favicon. |
| `render/emit.rs` | One AST node → HTML (the emitter). |
| `render/divs.rs` | `:::` fenced-div preprocessing + grouping into callouts/columns. |
| `render/figure.rs` | Standalone-image and captioned-cell `<figure>`s. |
| `render/theme.rs` | Theming: light/dark, `.css`/`.scss`, extension themes, the pre-paint script. |
| `render/deck.rs` | Slide-deck assembly on qmd-fast's own engine (reveal.js removed; native `.qmd-deck`/`.qmd-slides` + a `window.QmdDeck` API). |
| `render/extension/` | Format extensions (`_extensions/` themes/shortcodes) + shortcode expansion, in a single `mod.rs`. |
| `diff.rs` | Block-level diff (LCS over block ids) → `BlockOp`s. |
| `includes.rs` | `{{< include >}}` resolution + the per-file source map. |
| `math.rs` / `highlight.rs` | Server-side KaTeX / syntect, both offline. |
| `cite.rs` | Citations + cross-references + the IEEE-style bibliography. |
| `site/` | Multi-page projects: `config` (`_site.yml` model), `book`, `xref` (cross-page refs), `search` (cross-page index), and `mod` (discovery, chrome, page render). |
| `frontmatter.rs` | Front-matter parsing + unknown-key linting (the `closest()` did-you-mean). |
| `render/validate.rs` | Closed-vocabulary linting of cell `#|` options + callout kinds, each a located (click-to-source) `Warning`. |
| `schema.rs` | Bundled Draft-2020-12 JSON Schemas for front matter + `_site.yml`, emitted by `qmd-fast schema`. |

`crates/server/src`, the binary (`qmd-fast`):

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `main.rs` | CLI: the `preview` / `build` / `render` / `blocks` / `schema` subcommands. |
| `protocol.rs` | The shared websocket message contract (both servers + the client), defined once so they can't drift. |
| `serve.rs` | Single-document websocket server + file watcher (incl. the `--host` LAN token guard). |
| `serve_site.rs` | Multi-page site/book server (per-page state, cross-page nav, hot reload). |
| `exec.rs` | Runs a doc's code cells and splices outputs back as blocks (incremental: the first changed cell + everything downstream). |
| `kernel.rs` | The warm Jupyter kernel (ZMQ), reused across edits, with interrupt + timeout. |
| `freeze.rs` | The persistent `_freeze/` execution cache, keyed by a cumulative content hash. |
| `log.rs` | Colourised dev-server console output. |

`web-client/`, the browser preview (vanilla JS, no build step): `client.js`
(mounts blocks, applies ops, the dev menu, click-to-source), `search.js` (the
Cmd-K palette), `toc-spy.js` (the scrollspy). The core also ships JS *assets*
(`code-enhance.js` with the `window.qmdEnhancers` registry, `mermaid.js`) that
both the live client and the static build inject.

The next two chapters go deeper: [the rendering pipeline](rendering.qmd) (how a
`.qmd` becomes blocks) and [extending qmd-fast](extending.qmd) (the conventions,
how to add a feature, and the dev workflow).
